record.title: Slovenia prohibits non-exempt residents’ travel to red-listed countries until judicial stay
record.scope: Outbound red-list travel prohibition, including land departures
record.crossings: National land departures to listed countries/regions; not a closure of every gate
record.movement: Residents undertaking non-exempt trips to red-listed destinations.
record.exceptions: Vaccinated/recovered people and specified work, education, transport, transit, landholding and urgent categories subject to conditions.
record.imposing_authority: Slovenian Government; implementation by border police
record.enforcement: Legally enforceable prohibition; court stay verified, first subsequent physical crossing not observed.
record.consequences: Departure restriction challenged on movement, private-life and economic-rights grounds.
record.relationship: Distinct 2021 outbound policy from R3-EU-005’s March 2020 physical Italy-frontier closure.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Contain COVID-19 transmission during the Easter period.
record.context: Article 11 restricted departures by residents. The Constitutional Court suspended its enforcement before the planned 12 April expiry.
record.uncertainty: Endpoint is the published judicial stay, not proof of simultaneous barrier removal or repeal of inbound testing/quarantine.

historical.duration_note: Formal permission or repeal; operational continuity and first physical reopening are not established. Precise legal dates do not by themselves establish a continuous observed operational spell.
